index.subtitulo: Automation panel to configure, optimize and customize your Debian Linux quickly and safely.
index.card_guiado_desc_1: By clicking Start, you get access to sessions that optimize, configure and make your Debian installation more practical for everyday use.
index.card_guiado_desc_2: DAP is intuitive and explains every step clearly — but, by design, it does not back up your files. Although every command is tested, things can go wrong. So: read the tips carefully before applying any changes and, whenever possible, back up before moving forward.

primeiros-passos.descricao: Before any configuration, update the system and enable the essential repositories. These steps are prerequisites for all upcoming sessions.
primeiros-passos.apt_update_desc: Syncs the local package list with the configured Debian repositories. Always run this before installing anything.
primeiros-passos.apt_upgrade_desc: Updates every package already installed on the system, including security fixes and point releases.
primeiros-passos.deb822_desc: Debian 13 uses the modern .sources format (deb822) by default. If your system still uses the legacy /etc/apt/sources.list, this button converts it automatically using apt modernize-sources. If you are already on deb822, nothing changes.
primeiros-passos.non_free_desc: Adds the contrib, non-free and non-free-firmware components to the Debian repositories. Required for proprietary drivers, firmware and some codecs.
primeiros-passos.non_free_info: ℹ️ Debian 13 fresh installs already come with these components enabled. This button is for older installations converted to deb822 or Live ISOs that ship without them.
primeiros-passos.flatpak_titulo: 📦 Install Flatpak, Flathub and store integration
primeiros-passos.flatpak_desc: Installs the Flatpak runtime, adds the Flathub remote and installs the Flatpak backend for your desktop store (GNOME Software on GNOME, Plasma Discover on KDE). After this, Flathub apps appear directly in your store.
primeiros-passos.flatpak_info: ℹ️ On desktops without a native store, only Flatpak (command line) is installed.
primeiros-passos.backports_desc: Adds the trixie-backports repository. Backports brings newer versions of specific packages (kernel, Mesa, firmware) to Debian Stable without forcing a full upgrade.
primeiros-passos.backports_info: ℹ️ Backports packages do not receive official security support from the Debian Security Team. Install only if you need newer hardware support or a specific feature.
primeiros-passos.kernel_desc: Installs linux-image-amd64 and linux-headers-amd64 from backports. Provides newer kernel versions for recent hardware (Wi-Fi, GPUs, chipsets).
primeiros-passos.kernel_aviso: ⚠️ Requires backports to be enabled (previous block). The kernel from backports is not covered by the Debian Stable security team. Restart after installing to use the new kernel.
primeiros-passos.confirmar_reboot:
🔄 Restart the computer now?

Save all open work before continuing.
primeiros-passos.mesa_titulo: 🎮 Update Mesa and firmware from backports
primeiros-passos.mesa_desc: Updates every installed mesa-* package to the backports version and installs the full firmware-linux from backports, bringing updated firmware for GPU, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and other compatible peripherals.
primeiros-passos.mesa_aviso: ⚠️ Requires backports to be enabled (previous block). Newer Mesa improves performance and compatibility on AMD and Intel GPUs.
primeiros-passos.extrepo_desc: Installs extrepo, the official Debian tool for enabling third-party repositories (Brave, Google Chrome, Signal, Spotify, VSCode) securely. The DAP does not enable any third-party repository automatically — the tool is just made available.
primeiros-passos.locale_desc: Installs translation packages, the Portuguese (Brazil) spell checker and changes the system default locale. Live ISOs do not ship with PT-BR locale generated by default.
primeiros-passos.locale_aviso: ⚠️ Restart your computer after completing step 3 to apply the language changes everywhere.
primeiros-passos.i386_desc: Adds the i386 architecture to dpkg. Required for 32-bit packages, including Steam, Wine and some old programs.
primeiros-passos.i386_info: ℹ️ Enabling i386 increases the size of the apt index and the time of apt update. Only enable if you plan to use Steam, Wine or other 32-bit software.

aplicativos.descricao: Recommended software for everyday use. All installed via Flatpak (Flathub), except the ArtCraft Suite and RPM-based Remote Access Tools.
aplicativos.bloco1_desc: Tools to work with documents, notes, email and e-books.
aplicativos.bloco2_desc: Video, music and streaming players to consume content day to day.
aplicativos.bloco3_desc: Image editing, vector illustration, 3D modeling, CAD and 3D printing.
aplicativos.bloco4_desc: Browsers, video call apps and messengers.
aplicativos.bloco5_desc: Video editors, 3D modeling, audio editing and music production.
aplicativos.bloco6_desc: Tools to sync files with Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox and other services.
aplicativos.bloco7_desc: Tools to access and control other computers remotely, or to connect to Windows and Linux servers via RDP, VNC and other protocols. Ideal for tech support, accessing work machines and server administration.
aplicativos.bloco7_aviso: ⚠️ Note about Wayland: Debian 13 is migrating from X11 to Wayland. Some traditional remote control tools (AnyDesk, TeamViewer) still have issues in this environment — black screen, frozen cursor or no control. The tools listed below work well on Wayland.
aplicativos.affinity_desc: Affinity has no native Linux version. This button opens the AffinityOnLinux installer, a community project (not affiliated with Serif/Canva) that sets up a pre-configured Wine environment to run Affinity.
aplicativos.affinity_aviso: ⚠️ You must have purchased and downloaded the Affinity .exe installer from the official Serif/Canva website before using this — DAP only prepares the Wine environment and opens the community installer; that installer will ask for the .exe file at the right moment. It's a third-party project: if something doesn't work on your hardware, check their known issues page.
aplicativos.affinity_prereq: 📦 Prerequisite: PyQt6 is required for the installer interface. DAP checks and installs it automatically if needed.
aplicativos.bloco_artcraft_desc: These apps are developed in Rust, are open source, and are recent alternatives to Adobe products. Each app has its own specialty (photo editing, vector, video, lighting, printing, effects and design).
aplicativos.bloco_artcraft_aviso: ℹ️ About support: these are independent projects, maintained by community developers. If something doesn't work, report the bug directly in the GitHub repository of the affected project — DAP only installs the official packages published by them.
aplicativos.lightworks_aviso: ⚠️ Note: Lightworks is not installed via Flatpak. The button downloads the official RPM package from the LWKS website. On Debian, we recommend using DaVinci Resolve instead (not included in DAP).
aplicativos.rclone_aviso: ℹ️ Cloud account setup: Rclone Manager is a graphical interface for Rclone. It lets you configure access to Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, S3, and dozens of other cloud storage services. After installing, open Rclone Manager and follow the guide inside its interface to add your accounts. If you need the Rclone CLI, Rclone Manager itself offers an option to install it. Setting up the accounts is done by you, inside Rclone Manager.
aplicativos.rclone_uninstall_aviso: ⚠️ Completely remove Rclone Manager? This button removes the packages rclone-manager and rclone from the system, including any version of Rclone that Rclone Manager itself installed. Your cloud accounts are stored in ~/.config/rclone and are NOT deleted — if you reinstall later, your accounts will still be there. Irreversible action regarding the packages.

codecs.descricao: This session brings together what Debian needs to handle content that is not in the official repositories: media codecs, commercial DVD playback and Windows fonts (for compatibility with documents and programs that depend on them).
codecs.codecs_desc: Installs the complete set of Debian multimedia codecs, including essential GStreamer plugins and the non-free codec package from the non-free repository.
codecs.codecs_info: ℹ️ What this solves: videos in MP4, MKV, AVI, WebM and other formats play in any player (VLC, MPV, Firefox, Chromium). Without these codecs, many files simply won't open or will play without audio/video. It's also a prerequisite for video editing in tools like Kdenlive and Shotcut.
codecs.extras_titulo: Commercial DVD Playback and Additional Firmware
codecs.extras_desc: Installs libdvdcss2 (to read commercial DVDs with CSS protection) and the full firmware-linux package for hardware that depends on proprietary firmware.
codecs.extras_info: ℹ️ What this solves: without libdvdcss2, Debian cannot read commercial DVDs (with CSS protection) — only homemade DVDs or video files. firmware-linux complements the already installed firmware and covers devices that need restricted redistribution.
codecs.extras_aviso: ⚠️ libdvdcss2 is not in the official Debian repository for legal reasons. It is distributed by deb-multimedia, a third-party repository. Install only if you need to play commercial DVDs.
codecs.fontes_desc: Installs ttf-mscorefonts-installer (Arial, Times New Roman, Verdana, etc.) and the metric substitutes fonts-crosextra-caladea (for Cambria) and fonts-crosextra-carlito (for Calibri).
codecs.fontes_aviso: ⚠️ This process downloads and installs proprietary Microsoft fonts. Make sure you comply with the licensing terms.
codecs.fontes_info: ℹ️ Fonts installed: Arial, Times New Roman, Calibri, Cambria, Candara, Consolas, Constantia, Corbel, and others. What this solves: documents in LibreOffice, OnlyOffice and other programs look correct — without these fonts, the system substitutes alternatives that may break the formatting. The metric substitutes (caladea for Cambria, carlito for Calibri) fill gaps in the original MS package and are installed together.
codecs.fontconfig_desc: Applies an optimized fontconfig profile for LCD screens: antialiasing on, light hinting (hintslight), default lcd filter (lcddefault) and RGB subpixel.
codecs.fontconfig_info: ℹ️ What this solves: the default font rendering on Debian is often considered "harsh" or "blurry" by users coming from other distributions. This profile improves sharpness without changing letter spacing. It applies to your user (~/.config/fontconfig/fonts.conf), does not affect other users on the system.

hardware.descricao: Hardware-specific settings. Choose your GPU type below (AMD, NVIDIA or Intel) to see the corresponding drivers and tools. Each accordion detects your computer's hardware and tells you if the recommended drivers are already in use.
hardware.amd_detection_desc: Checks if the system has an AMD GPU or APU and tells you if the recommended driver (amdgpu) is already in use.
hardware.vulkan_desc: Installs the Vulkan libraries (32-bit and 64-bit versions), Mesa 3D with the RADV driver (AMD's open-source Vulkan driver), diagnostic tools and compatibility drivers. Essential for Steam, Proton and native games.
hardware.vaapi_desc: Hardware video acceleration drivers for smooth playback and encoding. On Debian, the mesa-va-drivers package already provides full AMD support — no extra repository needed.
hardware.corectrl_desc: GUI for fan, clock and voltage control on AMD GPUs.
hardware.lact_desc: Modern alternative to CoreCtrl for fan, clock and voltage control on AMD GPUs.
hardware.overclock_desc: Enables the amdgpu.ppfeaturemask kernel parameter, unlocking advanced clock and voltage adjustments in CoreCtrl and LACT.
hardware.overclock_aviso: ⚠️ Requires reboot. Only enable if you know what you're doing — bad overclock can cause instability.
hardware.nvidia_aviso: ⚠️ Without nvidia-drm.modeset=1, Wayland is unstable with NVIDIA cards. The non-free repository (Session 1) is a prerequisite. After installing anything here, reboot your computer.
hardware.nvidia_detection_desc: Checks if the system has an NVIDIA GPU, identifies its generation and tells you which driver Debian recommends.
hardware.nvidia_driver_desc: Detects your NVIDIA GPU generation and automatically installs the correct series — nvidia-open-kernel-dkms for Turing (RTX 20xx, GTX 16xx) or newer, nvidia-kernel-dkms for Maxwell, Pascal, Volta and older. Includes the required firmware and the nvidia-driver package with X11 and Wayland support.
hardware.nvidia_driver_info: ℹ️ About detection: DAP uses nvidia-detect (official Debian package) to identify the exact generation. If the package is not installed, it falls back to lspci with a model heuristic. Installing the wrong series (e.g., nvidia-open-kernel-dkms on a GTX 750 Ti) results in a black screen after reboot — this detection prevents that.
hardware.nvidia_confirmar_reverter:
⚠️ Revert the NVIDIA driver?

The system will go back to using the nouveau driver (open-source, included in Debian by default).

Gaming and 3D application performance will be reduced until you reinstall the proprietary driver.

Continue?
hardware.nvidia_cuda_desc: Installs the CUDA libraries and hardware encoding libraries (NVENC/NVDEC) so OBS, Kdenlive, FFmpeg and other programs can use the GPU for video encoding.
hardware.nvidia_modeset_desc: Enables the nvidia-drm.modeset=1 kernel parameter, required for Wayland to work correctly with NVIDIA cards.
hardware.intel_aviso: ⚠️ These packages are for Intel iGPUs (integrated graphics). If you have a dedicated AMD or NVIDIA GPU, the dedicated card's driver handles most acceleration — the Intel drivers may still be useful if you use the iGPU in tandem, but they're not mandatory.
hardware.intel_detection_desc: Checks if the system has an Intel iGPU and tells you if the recommended driver (i915 or xe) is already in use.
hardware.intel_media_desc: The intel-media-va-driver and intel-media-va-driver-non-free packages enable hardware video acceleration on Intel iGPUs Skylake (6th generation) or newer. This reduces CPU usage when watching 4K videos, using the browser and editing video. Older chips (Haswell or earlier) use the i965 driver, which already ships with Debian.

notes.nvidia: For Turing (RTX 20xx / GTX 16xx) or newer GPUs, the open-kernel driver is recommended by Debian 13. For Maxwell, Pascal, Volta and older, the classic proprietary driver is required.
notes.amd_gpu: Mesa, RADV and VA-API on Debian already come with full AMD support. No need for 'freeworld' packages like on Fedora.
notes.amd_apu: AMD APUs with integrated graphics (Ryzen with Radeon Vega, RDNA or RDNA2). Debian's Mesa already covers everything.
notes.intel_gpu: For Intel iGPUs Skylake (6th generation) or newer. The non-free package brings the complete VA-API driver. Haswell and older chips use i965, which already ships with Debian.
notes.broadcom_wifi: The broadcom-sta-dkms driver conflicts with open-source drivers (brcmfmac, b43). Only install if Wi-Fi doesn't work with Debian's default drivers.
notes.realtek_ethernet: The kernel's r8169 driver covers almost every Realtek card. The firmware-realtek package brings additional firmware for recent models.

dispositivos-perifericos.descricao: Detects hardware that may need additional drivers or firmware (not included in Debian for licensing reasons), offers safe supplements, and lets you configure specific peripherals. Nothing is installed automatically — each suggestion has separate install and revert buttons.
dispositivos-perifericos.deteccao_desc: Click the button below to scan your computer. DAP will identify GPUs, network cards and USB adapters that may need additional drivers, cross-referencing hardware IDs against a community-maintained map. Nothing is installed automatically — each suggestion appears as a separate card, with explicit install and revert buttons.
dispositivos-perifericos.suplementos_desc: These packages complement Debian's standard linux-firmware. They are safe to install on any system — they don't conflict with existing drivers and cover hardware that Red Hat doesn't distribute for licensing reasons or because it's outside Debian's scope.
dispositivos-perifericos.firmware_vendor_desc: The firmware-linux package brings firmware that isn't in Debian's main package — recent Realtek Wi-Fi chips (RTL8852), some Intel models, and vendor firmware that requires restricted redistribution. It complements linux-firmware, it doesn't replace it.
dispositivos-perifericos.copr_aviso:
⚠️ Attention before continuing:
• These drivers are hardware-specific — only install if you have the indicated device.
• Some replace the kernel's open-source driver (e.g., broadcom-sta-dkms replaces brcmfmac). This can break a working Wi-Fi.
• If you don't know whether you need it, use the automatic detection in the accordion above first — it identifies the exact model.
• All drivers here are in Debian's official repositories (main, non-free or non-free-firmware) — no COPR or third-party repo dependencies.
dispositivos-perifericos.broadcom_desc: Proprietary broadcom-sta-dkms driver for Broadcom Wi-Fi chips (common in old laptops and MacBooks). Lives in Debian's non-free. Only install if the open-source driver (brcmfmac/b43) doesn't work.
dispositivos-perifericos.confirmar_reverter_tudo:
⚠️ Attention!

You are about to fully revert this item:

• The package will be uninstalled
• The repository will be removed
• Group changes (if any) will be undone

If you depend on this driver (for example, a Wi-Fi adapter or controller), you'll lose functionality.

Continue?
dispositivos-perifericos.input_add_desc: Required for Steam Input, xpadneo and controller drivers to recognize the user. Works for Xbox, PlayStation and Nintendo controllers using kernel drivers.
dispositivos-perifericos.input_add_aviso: ℹ️ Requires logout/login to take effect.
dispositivos-perifericos.steam_devices_desc: Installs the udev rules from the steam-devices package, which allow the system to correctly recognize Xbox, PlayStation and Nintendo controllers when used with Steam.
dispositivos-perifericos.steam_devices_info: ℹ️ What this solves: without these rules, some controllers may not be detected by Steam even when connected. It's a small package that complements the input group above — the group gives your user permission, and this package teaches the system to identify each controller model.
dispositivos-perifericos.aviso_rpmfusion_corpo: Some drivers (NVIDIA, Broadcom) require the non-free repository. Enable it in the First Steps session before installing these drivers.
dispositivos-perifericos.aviso_secureboot_corpo: To use the NVIDIA driver, you need to register the MOK key during installation or disable Secure Boot. Without that, the driver won't load and the machine may boot in minimal resolution.
dispositivos-perifericos.sem_dispositivos: No device with an additional driver suggestion was detected. Your hardware works with Debian's default drivers.
dispositivos-perifericos.ja_funciona: This device already works with the standard driver ({driver}). We don't recommend installing the proprietary driver — it can cause conflicts.
dispositivos-perifericos.ja_instalado: The suggested driver is already installed on this system.
dispositivos-perifericos.precisa_driver: This device may need the {pkg} package. Install it if the hardware isn't working correctly.
dispositivos-perifericos.repo_necessario: This driver lives in Debian's {repo} repository. Enable it in First Steps before installing.

notes.nvidia: Requires non-free repository. DAP tries to use nvidia-detect to identify the exact generation and suggest the correct package (nvidia-open-kernel-dkms or nvidia-kernel-dkms).
notes.amd_gpu: Hardware video acceleration (VA-API) on AMD GPUs. Debian's Mesa already supports this natively.
notes.amd_apu: AMD APUs with integrated graphics (Ryzen with Radeon Vega or RDNA).
notes.intel_gpu: Video acceleration on Intel iGPUs Skylake (6th gen) or newer. Older chips (Haswell or earlier) use the i965 driver, already in Debian.
notes.broadcom_wifi: Only install if the open-source driver (brcmfmac/b43) doesn't work. broadcom-sta-dkms conflicts with them and can take down a working Wi-Fi.
notes.realtek_ethernet: Alternative driver for Realtek Ethernet cards. The default driver (r8169) works in most cases — only install firmware-realtek if the cable isn't recognized.

dispositivos-perifericos.confirmar_reverter:
⚠️ Attention!

You are about to revert a driver.

If the device depends on this driver to work (for example, a Wi-Fi adapter), you will lose functionality after reboot.

Have an alternative connection available before continuing.

Continue?

gaming.descricao: Installs the main launchers, Windows compatibility tools (Wine/Proton), performance and monitoring utilities, and provides ready-to-use tips to optimize the gaming experience on Debian.
gaming.launchers_desc: Install the main game launchers for Debian.
gaming.launchers_info: ℹ️ Steam is installed natively via the non-free repository (requires the i386 architecture, enabled in First Steps). Heroic and Lutris via Flatpak.
gaming.steam_nativo_info: ℹ️ Native Steam: requires i386 architecture active (First Steps session). If you had Steam via Flatpak in previous versions, remove it manually with flatpak uninstall -y com.valvesoftware.Steam to avoid duplication. Your games live in ~/.steam/ and are preserved.
gaming.compat_desc: Tools to run Windows games and programs outside of Steam, and resources that help with compatibility.
gaming.compat_info_extra: ℹ️ Winetricks installs extra components (fonts, libraries) inside a Wine prefix. Bottles is a modern alternative to plain Wine, with visual management of "bottles" (prefixes) and support for Proton-GE runners.
gaming.ntsync_info: ℹ️ About NTSYNC: Debian 13 (Trixie) ships kernel 6.12, which does not yet include the NTSYNC module (it entered kernel 6.14). Debian's Wine also doesn't have NTSYNC enabled. Because of this, DAP does not install NTSYNC in this version — the feature would be useless without the prerequisites. If you install a newer kernel (via backports, testing, etc.), NTSYNC will work automatically for Wine and Proton.
gaming.performance_desc: Tools that optimize performance during gameplay and allow monitoring FPS, CPU/GPU usage and other metrics.
gaming.performance_info_extra: ℹ️ GameMode sets CPU/GPU to maximum priority while a game is running. MangoHud shows an FPS/CPU/GPU overlay inside the game. Goverlay is a graphical interface to configure MangoHud without editing text files. Gamescope is a Valve micro-compositor that enables upscaling (FSR/NIS), FPS limiting, HDR and more.
gaming.gamescope_nvidia_flatpak_aviso: ⚠️ Gamescope + NVIDIA + Flatpak — attention: Gamescope was designed by Valve for the Mesa architecture (AMD/Intel). On NVIDIA cards with the proprietary driver, it can present instability — black screen, frozen cursor or the game closing on open. Additionally, native Gamescope (installed via apt) has difficulty interacting with games that run inside the Flatpak sandbox, and vice versa. Recommendation: keep everything in the same format. If you use Steam/Heroic via Flatpak, prefer also installing the Flatpak Gamescope extensions; if you use native Steam, prefer native Gamescope. On NVIDIA GPUs, if Gamescope doesn't work well, consider using MangoHud + GameMode as an alternative — they don't have this limitation.
gaming.avancado_desc: Tools for those who want to get the most out of Debian for gaming: specific Proton versions, image post-processing, performance presets and a controller test utility.
gaming.protonup_desc: Graphical interface that downloads and manages Proton-GE versions (community version of Proton, with extra fixes), plus runners for Lutris and Bottles.
gaming.protonup_info: ℹ️ After installing, open ProtonUp-Qt, choose the recommended Proton-GE version and click "Download". The latest version usually works well for most games.
gaming.vkbasalt_desc: Post-processing layer that adds sharpening, vibrance, FXAA, SMAA and other visual effects directly to Vulkan output. Useful for games that look a bit blurry by default.
gaming.vkbasalt_aviso: ⚠️ How to use: after installing, each game needs to enable vkBasalt individually. On Steam, add ENABLE_VKBASALT=1 %command% to the game's launch options. Outside Steam, set the ENABLE_VKBASALT=1 variable before running.
gaming.gamemode_presets_desc: Creates ready-to-use config files for MangoHud (FPS overlay) and GameMode (CPU/GPU priority). You get a clean, readable overlay without configuring anything manually.
gaming.gamemode_presets_info: ℹ️ Files are created at ~/.config/MangoHud/MangoHud.conf and ~/.config/gamemode.ini. If you already have custom files, they'll be overwritten — back them up beforehand if needed.
gaming.controller_test_desc: Installs a graphical tool to test buttons, analog stick dead zones, trigger response and controller rumble. Useful for diagnosing controllers with drift or buttons that don't respond.
gaming.emuladores_desc: Emulators for classic and modern consoles on Debian. All available via Flatpak.
gaming.emuladores_aviso_geral: ⚠️ Important notice: some emulators require BIOS, firmware or system files dumped from the original console to work. DAP does not provide these files for legal reasons. Consult each emulator's official documentation for how to obtain them from your own console.
gaming.retroarch_desc: Universal emulation frontend that runs dozens of consoles via "cores" (plugins). A single app for SNES, Mega Drive, NES, Game Boy, GBA, PS1 and many others.
gaming.retroarch_info: ℹ️ How to install cores: after opening RetroArch, use the Online Updater → Core Downloader menu to download the cores you want (snes9x, genesis_plus_gx, nestopia, mgba, beetle_psx, mupen64plus_next, etc).
gaming.dolphin_desc: Mature and very compatible emulator for GameCube and Wii. Runs most games at higher resolution than the original, with upscaling.
gaming.pcsx2_desc: PlayStation 2 emulator with upscaling support, widescreen patches and high compatibility with the console's catalog.
gaming.pcsx2_aviso: ⚠️ Requires PlayStation 2 BIOS. The BIOS must be dumped from your own console. DAP does not provide this file. After installing, consult the PCSX2 documentation for where to place the BIOS.
gaming.rpcs3_desc: PlayStation 3 emulator under active development. Compatibility varies per game — some run perfectly, others still have issues. Check the official compatibility list before installing.
gaming.rpcs3_aviso: ⚠️ Requires PlayStation 3 firmware. The firmware must be downloaded from Sony's official website (Sony provides firmware publicly for console updates) and installed by RPCS3 itself. DAP does not download or install this file.
gaming.rpcs3_info_extra: ℹ️ About the "unofficial build" notice: RPCS3 may show a message on first run indicating it was installed from an unofficial package. This is a warning from the emulator itself — the Flathub Flatpak is the official distribution channel for RPCS3 on Linux, and the warning does not affect functionality.
gaming.duckstation_desc: Modern and lightweight PlayStation 1 emulator, with high resolution support, graphical filters and support for modern controllers. A more user-friendly alternative to the classic ePSXe.
gaming.duckstation_aviso: ⚠️ May require PlayStation 1 BIOS. Although Duckstation has a built-in HLE BIOS (works without BIOS for many games), some titles require the real BIOS to function correctly. The BIOS must be dumped from your own console.
gaming.anticheat_desc: Informational panel about which anti-cheats work on Linux, which don't, and why. Nothing here is installed or executed — it's just for you to know before buying or trying a game.
gaming.dicas_desc: Recommended settings to get the most out of games on Debian.
gaming.dicas_aviso_steam: 💡 Steam — Launch Options: you can add commands to each game's launch options (right-click the game → Properties → Launch Options). Examples:
gaming.dicas_nota: ℹ️ Replace the -W and -H values with the desired resolution. -r 60 limits FPS to 60 — remove it if you want unlimited FPS.

casa-escritorio.descricao: Settings to get Debian ready for home and office use: printer, file sharing with Windows/phone, password manager and PDF reading with OCR. All in independent blocks — use only what you need.
casa-escritorio.cups_desc: Installs Debian's printing system (CUPS), support for automatic network printer discovery (Avahi/Bonjour) and generic drivers. After installing, most modern printers are recognized automatically in Settings → Printers.
casa-escritorio.cups_info: ℹ️ What is installed: cups, cups-filters, avahi-daemon, system-config-printer (management GUI) and ghostscript (format conversion). The CUPS service is enabled automatically.
casa-escritorio.cups_info_drivers: ℹ️ About specific drivers: HP printers may need hplip, Brother needs brother-* (from the manufacturer's site), Epson needs epson-inkjet-printer-escpr. After installing CUPS, open Printer Settings — the system suggests the missing drivers.
casa-escritorio.compart_desc: Tools to transfer and share files between Debian and other devices. Choose according to your case: Windows on the local network (Samba), Android/iPhone (LocalSend) or Linux network (Warpinator).
casa-escritorio.samba_desc: Installs Samba, which allows sharing Debian folders with Windows computers on the same network — and also accessing Windows shared folders from Debian.
casa-escritorio.samba_aviso: ⚠️ After installing: open Nautilus/Dolphin, right-click a folder → Properties → Sharing (or Folder Sharing) and check "Share this folder". Debian takes care of the rest.
casa-escritorio.samba_info: ℹ️ What is installed: samba, samba-client and cifs-utils (to mount Windows folders). The smbd and nmbd services are enabled.
casa-escritorio.localsend_desc: Cross-platform app (Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS) that sends files between devices on the same local network. It's the modern alternative to AirDrop — works across any combination of systems, with a simple interface.
casa-escritorio.localsend_info: ℹ️ How to use: install LocalSend on Debian (via DAP) and on your phone (via app store). Open both on the same Wi-Fi network, and the devices find each other automatically. No account, no cloud, no ads.
casa-escritorio.warpinator_desc: File transfer tool from Linux Mint, available for Debian. Simple and direct: open it, it finds other Warpinator devices on the network and transfers files with one click. Ideal if you have more than one Linux at home.
casa-escritorio.warpinator_info: ℹ️ When to use: if the destination is also Linux, Warpinator is often faster than LocalSend (less overhead). For phone, use LocalSend.
casa-escritorio.keepassxc_desc: Local, open-source, cloud-free password manager. Stores everything in an encrypted .kdbx file on your computer — you decide if you sync it (via Nextcloud, Syncthing, USB drive, etc). Integrates with browsers and supports autofill.
casa-escritorio.keepassxc_info: ℹ️ Why KeePassXC instead of Bitwarden? KeePassXC is 100% offline and local — nothing leaves your computer. Ideal for those who prefer not to depend on any service. If you prefer cloud convenience, Bitwarden is also a good option (but DAP installs KeePassXC, which is more aligned with the local-first philosophy).
casa-escritorio.okular_tesseract_titulo: Okular + Tesseract — PDF Reader with OCR
casa-escritorio.okular_tesseract_desc: Installs Okular (PDF, e-book and comic reader, very fast) and Tesseract (OCR engine). With both, you can open a scanned PDF (image) and extract the text — useful for copying excerpts from scanned documents.
casa-escritorio.okular_tesseract_info: ℹ️ What is OCR: Optical Character Recognition — converts text images (scanned, photographed) into searchable and copyable text. Tesseract supports Portuguese, English and 100+ languages. In Okular, use Tools → Text Selection on scanned PDFs (with Tesseract installed, it recognizes automatically).
casa-escritorio.okular_tesseract_info_lang: ℹ️ Additional OCR languages: we install the base package with Portuguese and English. If you need another language, look for tesseract-ocr-XX in the package manager.

diagnostico.descricao: Visual panel of system state. Shows in real time what's happening with CPU, memory, disk and services — without needing to open the terminal. Useful for investigating slowness, disk usage, temperature and recent errors.
diagnostico.aviso_geral: ℹ️ This panel is read-only. No command here changes the system — they're all queries. If you want to fix something specific, the actions are in the other DAP sessions.
diagnostico.painel_desc: Data collected from DAP's local endpoints. Some values update automatically; others can be updated manually.
diagnostico.top5_desc: Processes consuming the most CPU and memory right now.
diagnostico.otimizacoes_desc: Shows the current state of the performance tunings that can be applied in the Tunings and Maintenance session. Values in green indicate the tuning is active; neutral values indicate Debian's default. This section is informational only — to apply or revert a tuning, use the buttons in the corresponding session.
diagnostico.otimizacoes_info: ℹ️ About the values: this section only shows what's currently active. Each tuning is reversible and can be applied or reverted individually in the Tunings and Maintenance session. If a tuning is blank or shows "N/A", the feature may not be available on this kernel — it's not an error.
diagnostico.armazen_desc: See how much space each partition is using. Useful when the system warns "disk full" or when you don't know what's eating up space.
diagnostico.particoes_desc: Lists mounted partitions with usage, free space and mount point.
diagnostico.saude_desc: Disk health check (HDDs and SSDs) via SMART and reading component temperatures (CPU, GPU, motherboard). Helps detect problems before they become serious failure.
diagnostico.gsmart_desc: Installs GSmartControl, a graphical interface for smartctl. It shows disk health, temperature, hours of use, bad sectors, and allows running quick and extended tests with a click.
diagnostico.gsmart_info: ℹ️ How to interpret: in the "Health" column, a green ✅ means a healthy disk. A red ❌ means failure — back up immediately. Temperatures above 55°C under continuous use deserve attention.
diagnostico.gsmart_info_root: ℹ️ About the password: when opening GSmartControl, it may ask for administrator password to read SMART data — this is normal (the smartctl needs access to the physical device). The password window comes from the system, not from DAP.
diagnostico.coolercontrol_desc: Installs CoolerControl, a complete monitoring and thermal control center. In addition to showing temperatures, fan speeds and other sensors in real time, it lets you create custom fan curves (for example, "when the GPU reaches 60°C, spin the fan at 50%"). It's the most robust thermal management tool for Debian.
diagnostico.coolercontrol_info:
ℹ️ What you can do with it:
  • View temperatures of CPU, GPU and motherboard in real time
  • View speed (RPM) of all system fans
  • Create custom fan curves based on any sensor
  • Configure alerts for high temperatures or fan failures
  • Build dashboards with the data you use the most
diagnostico.coolercontrol_info_repo: ℹ️ About installation: CoolerControl is not in Debian's standard repositories. We use the project's official repository, maintained by the developer.
diagnostico.coolercontrol_info_group: ℹ️ About permissions: DAP adds your user to the coolercontrol group so the GUI can control fans without asking for a password on every action. That group only takes effect after logging out and back in. The daemon starts working immediately.
diagnostico.coolercontrol_info_sensors: ℹ️ If a sensor doesn't appear: CoolerControl uses the same sensors as lm-sensors. If a sensor is missing, open the terminal and run sudo sensors-detect, answering "YES" to all questions. Then restart the service: sudo systemctl restart coolercontrold.
diagnostico.journal_desc: Filters the systemd journal for error messages from the last 24 hours and groups them by origin — so you quickly see if something is failing repeatedly without having to read the raw log.
diagnostico.journal_info: ℹ️ Important: not every error in the journal is a problem. Services that try to start before the hardware is ready, or drivers that report warnings during boot, are normal. Use this panel to detect patterns: the same error appearing dozens of times indicates something that needs attention.

producao-multimidia.descricao: Tools to record, edit, stream and produce audio and video content on Debian.
producao-multimidia.obs_titulo: 🎬 OBS Studio - Installation and Virtual Camera
producao-multimidia.obs_desc: Install OBS Studio for recording/streaming and enable the virtual camera for video calls.
producao-multimidia.obs_aviso: ⚠️ The virtual camera requires Secure Boot to be configured correctly or disabled.
producao-multimidia.easyeffects_desc: Sound effects processor for PipeWire to apply noise reduction and equalization.

virtualizacao.descricao: Tools to run virtual machines on Debian. QEMU/KVM is the native stack (most performant) and GNOME Boxes simplifies the experience for beginners.
virtualizacao.qemu_desc: Native Linux virtualization stack. Runs virtual machines with hardware acceleration via KVM — it's the most performant option. Installs QEMU, the libvirt daemon, virt-manager (graphical interface) and configures the default network.
virtualizacao.qemu_info: ℹ️ About permissions: your user is added to the libvirt group so you can manage VMs without a password on every action. The group only takes effect after logout/login — until then, virt-manager will ask for the administrator password when opening.
virtualizacao.qemu_info_network: ℹ️ About the default network: on Debian, the libvirt default network needs to be started and set to autostart (on Fedora this is automatic). DAP does this for you.
virtualizacao.boxes_desc: Simplified graphical interface to create and manage virtual machines. Uses QEMU/KVM under the hood, so it's as performant as virt-manager — the difference is the experience: instead of configuring CPU, RAM and disk separately, you point to an .iso file and it handles the rest.
virtualizacao.boxes_info: ℹ️ Recommended for: those starting with virtualization and wanting to test a Linux distribution or Windows without manually configuring anything. If you're already experienced, prefer virt-manager — it offers more control over the VM.

ajustes-manutencao.descricao: Optional performance and audio tunings, basic system settings (APT, dual-boot) and periodic Debian maintenance tools.
ajustes-manutencao.tuning_desc: Recommended adjustments to improve system responsiveness in games and general use. Each item is independent and can be reverted at any time.
ajustes-manutencao.vm_max_map_count_titulo: Memory Adjustments for Games and Heavy Applications
ajustes-manutencao.vm_max_map_count_desc: Increases the maximum number of memory areas each process can map. Debian's default is 65530, insufficient for modern games — several titles fail to launch or crash due to lack of mappable memory (Hogwarts Legacy, Counter-Strike 2, The Finals, Star Citizen, among others).
ajustes-manutencao.vm_max_map_count_info: ℹ️ What changes: the limit goes from 65,530 to 2,147,483,642 (the practical maximum). It's a compatibility fix, not a "tweak".
ajustes-manutencao.vm_swappiness_cache_desc: Adjusts two kernel parameters that control swap and file cache. Debian ships with conservative values; these adjustments make the system keep more RAM available for foreground applications and retain disk caches longer.
ajustes-manutencao.tcp_bbr_desc: Replaces the default TCP congestion control algorithm (cubic) with BBR, developed by Google. It improves latency and throughput on connections with packet loss — benefits online gaming, streaming and downloads.
ajustes-manutencao.audio_tuning_desc: Adjustments that improve the experience for those who record, produce or game with real-time audio. Recommended for users of Ardour, LMMS, Reaper or those who stream with live monitoring.
ajustes-manutencao.realtime_setup_desc: Configures the system to allow audio applications to have real-time priority. Without this, audio may present glitches (crackling or xruns) under load.
ajustes-manutencao.realtime_setup_info:
ℹ️ What changes:
• realtime group created with adequate memory limits.
• Your user added to this group — requires logout/login.
• Configuration files installed by the realtime-setup package (from the Debian repository).
ajustes-manutencao.realtime_setup_aviso: ⚠️ Requires logout/login: the realtime group only takes effect after you log out and back in.
ajustes-manutencao.pipewire_quantum_desc: Reduces the PipeWire quantum (audio buffer size) from 1024 to 256 samples. Reduces audio latency from ~21ms to ~5ms — essential for recording and games with positional audio.
ajustes-manutencao.pipewire_quantum_info:
ℹ️ What changes:
• Creates ~/.config/pipewire/pipewire.conf.d/99-dap-quantum.conf.
• Restarts pipewire, pipewire-pulse and wireplumber.
• Applies immediately — no reboot.
• Trade-off: lower latency uses slightly more CPU. On modest machines, it can cause crackling.
ajustes-manutencao.apt_desc: Configures APT to download multiple packages in parallel, speeding up large upgrades.
ajustes-manutencao.apt_info_extra: ℹ️ The setting will be applied with the selected value. You can reapply with different values at any time.
ajustes-manutencao.dual_boot_desc: Makes Debian use the hardware clock in local time (the same way Windows does by default), fixing the wrong time when switching between systems.
ajustes-manutencao.dual_boot_aviso: 💡 By default, Windows stores the hardware clock in local time, while Linux (Debian) stores it in UTC. This button configures Debian to use local time, matching Windows' behavior — so you don't need to change anything on Windows.
ajustes-manutencao.dual_boot_confirmar:
⚠️ Adjust the clock to local time?

This will make Debian use local time (like Windows). The change may cause a temporary jump of a few hours in the clock.

Continue?
ajustes-manutencao.manutencao_debian_desc: Periodic tasks that keep the system clean and controllable: cache cleanup, kernel management and GRUB settings.
ajustes-manutencao.limpeza_desc: Cleans the APT cache, orphaned dependencies and unused Flatpak runtimes.
ajustes-manutencao.kernel_desc: Manage the kernels installed on your system.
ajustes-manutencao.kernel_aviso: ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Removing an older kernel version is not recommended — Debian keeps at least the current and previous version.
ajustes-manutencao.kernel_msg_atual_nao_removivel:
❌ Cannot remove the kernel you are currently using ({kernel}).

Reboot with another kernel before removing this one.
ajustes-manutencao.kernel_confirmar_remocao:
⚠️ WARNING!

You are about to remove the kernel:
{kernel}

Are you sure you want to continue?
ajustes-manutencao.grub_desc: Configure GRUB to always show when the computer turns on and set the display time to 10 seconds.
ajustes-manutencao.grub_aviso: ⚠️ This change affects system boot. Make sure GRUB is installed correctly.
ajustes-manutencao.grub_confirmar_recomendado:
⚠️ Apply the recommended GRUB configuration?

• GRUB will always show on boot
• Display time: 10 seconds
ajustes-manutencao.grub_confirmar_padrao: Restore default GRUB configuration (timeout=5 seconds, hidden)?

estado-debian.descricao: Debian-specific information and tools: installed version check, variant detection (Stable/Testing/Sid) and AppArmor — Debian's default mandatory access control system.
estado-debian.aviso_geral: ℹ️ This session is informative. Commands here only read system state. Nothing is changed without you explicitly clicking a button — and the ones that do change make clear what they do.
estado-debian.versao_desc: DAP is developed and tested on Debian 13 (Trixie). If you're on a different version, some commands may behave unexpectedly (renamed packages, changed repositories, new syntax). This check warns you when that happens.
estado-debian.versao_info: ℹ️ Supported versions: Debian 13 (Trixie) and newer. Older versions (12 Bookworm and earlier) may require manual adjustments. DAP keeps working, but you may need to adapt a specific command.
estado-debian.variante_desc: Debian has three main channels: Stable (recommended for general use), Testing (pre-release) and Sid/Unstable (development). There are also derivative distributions (MX Linux, LMDE, Kali, Raspberry Pi OS). DAP was developed for pure Debian Stable.
estado-debian.variante_info: ℹ️ Why this matters: DAP installs packages that are in stable repositories. If you're on Testing/Sid, some packages may not exist or have different names. This detection warns you before you try something that won't work.
estado-debian.apparmor_desc: AppArmor is Debian's default mandatory access control system. It restricts what each program can do based on per-application profiles — simpler than Fedora's SELinux and enabled by default since Debian 10.
estado-debian.apparmor_status_desc: Shows the current AppArmor state (enabled/disabled) and how many profiles are loaded.
estado-debian.apparmor_status_info:
ℹ️ What AppArmor does:
  • Active — profiles loaded and blocking accesses outside allowed. It's Debian's default and recommended.
  • Inactive — no profiles loaded. Reduces system security. Investigate before enabling.
estado-debian.apparmor_profiles_desc: Lists the AppArmor profiles that are loaded on the system. Useful to know which programs are being monitored by AppArmor.
estado-debian.apparmor_desabilitar_desc: Many tutorials on the internet recommend disabling AppArmor when something doesn't work. This is not a good practice on Debian — the system is designed to work with it enabled, and disabling masks problems instead of solving them.
estado-debian.apparmor_desabilitar_info: ℹ️ If you need to disable it permanently: edit /etc/default/grub and add apparmor=0 to the GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT line, then run sudo update-grub. DAP does not do this automatically — it's your decision.

sobre-dap.sobre_o_que: Debian Advantage Panel (DAP) is a visual automation panel for configuring Debian Linux. It brings together, in a friendly interface, the steps that would normally require terminal commands — from the initial system tuning to getting everything ready for daily use. It was designed especially for those who installed Debian from a Live ISO and need to complete the system (locale, codecs, drivers, repositories, apps).
sobre-dap.sobre_porque: Debian is excellent, but it requires some initial steps (enabling the contrib, non-free and non-free-firmware repositories, installing codecs, configuring drivers, generating the locale) that often intimidate users coming from other distributions. DAP automates those steps and presents them clearly, in guided sessions — without you having to remember commands or search for tutorials.
sobre-dap.sobre_ganhos: With DAP, you get your Debian complete in a few clicks: PT-BR locale, spell checker, multimedia codecs, essential repositories, AMD/NVIDIA/Intel drivers, graphics acceleration, gaming support (Steam, Heroic, Lutris, Proton), productivity tools, internet apps, audio and video editing, and much more. All with real-time logs and without needing to open the terminal.
sobre-dap.sobre_nao_faz_1: It does not replace the terminal — when something goes wrong, some problems still require manual commands for diagnosis.
sobre-dap.sobre_nao_faz_2: It does not install games — it prepares the system for you to install and run games, but does not download or install games themselves.
sobre-dap.sobre_nao_faz_3: It does not back up your data — we always recommend having snapshots or a backup before making system changes.
sobre-dap.sobre_nao_faz_4: It is not affiliated with the Debian Project or SPI — it is an independent project maintained by the community.
sobre-dap.sobre_nao_faz_5: It is not an operating system installer — DAP configures an already-installed Debian, it does not install Debian from scratch.

sobre-dap.atualizar_info: ℹ️ Updating keeps your settings and history.
